To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 50-% delay of cascaded transmission line is not constant and it can be estimated using the first order RC-circuit.
the 50-% time delay is an interesting parameter to characterize a TL.
the 50-% time-delay of the cascaded lines is a function of the line length, of the load and of the source impedance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the accurate modeling and the measurement of signal integrity for high-rate microelectronics interconnection.
the development of a new model of high-rate SI for the accurate characterization of the microstrip line.
the development and the validation of a new model to characterize high-speed interconnect line.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 50-% delay-time of a cascaded interconnection is a function of both the line length and the load impedance.
the 50-% delay-time is an important parameter for SI analysis.
a propagation-time of about 50% of the signal duration is a good compromise between the signal integrity and the power consumption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 50-% propagation-delay assessment is proposed and validated for the cascaded interconnect line.
the accurate modeling and measurements of high-speed interconnect line are presented and validated.
the proposed method can be used for the high-rate interconnection signal integrity analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple first-order RC-circuit is able to predict the 50-% of propagation-time for cascaded transmission lines.
the 50-% delay-time is not the same as the time delay of the first order RC-circuit.
the 50-% delay time is a very useful tool to predict the signal integrity of the high-speed interconnect lines.
